exercises.instruction: Make one sentence from two. Use the words in brackets to make a relative clause (Type 2). You will need to use who/whom/whose/which/where.

items.prompt: Catherine is very friendly. (She lives next door to us.)
answers: Catherine, who lives next door to us, is very friendly.

items.prompt: We stayed at the Park Hotel. (A friend of ours recommended this hotel.)
answers: We stayed at the Park Hotel, which a friend of ours recommended.

items.prompt: We drove to the airport. (The airport was not far from the city.)
answers: We drove to the airport, which was not far from the city.

items.prompt: Kate’s husband is an airline pilot. (I have never met Kate’s husband.)
answers: Kate’s husband, who I’ve never met, is an airline pilot.
Kate’s husband, whom I’ve never met, is an airline pilot.

items.prompt: Lisa is away from home a lot. (Lisa’s job involves a lot of travelling.)
answers: Lisa, whose job involves a lot of travelling, is away from home a lot.

items.prompt: Paul and Emily have a daughter, Alice. (Alice has just started school.)
answers: Paul and Emily have a daughter, Alice, who has just started school.

items.prompt: The new stadium will hold 90,000 spectators. (The stadium will be finished next month.)
answers: The new stadium, which will be finished next month, will hold 90,000 spectators.

items.prompt: My brother lives in Alaska. (Alaska is the largest state in the US.)
answers: My brother lives in Alaska, which is the largest state in the US.

items.prompt: Our teacher was very kind. (I have forgotten her name.)
answers: Our teacher, whose name I have forgotten, was very kind.

items.prompt: We enjoyed our visit to the museum. (We saw a lot of interesting things in the museum.)
answers: We enjoyed our visit to the museum, where we saw a lot of interesting things.

exercises.instruction: Each item gives a sentence and a fact in brackets. Write the whole sentence again with a relative clause of Type 1 or Type 2. Use commas where necessary.

items.prompt: My brother is an architect. (He lives in Hong Kong.)
answers: My brother, who lives in Hong Kong, is an architect.

items.prompt: The strike at the factory has now ended. (The strike began ten days ago.)
answers: The strike at the factory, which began ten days ago, has now ended.

items.prompt: I was looking for a book this morning. (I’ve found it now.)
answers: I’ve found the book I was looking for this morning.
I’ve found the book that/which I was looking for this morning.

items.prompt: I’ve had my car for 15 years. (This car has never broken down.)
answers: My car, which I’ve had for 15 years, has never broken down.

items.prompt: A lot of people applied for the job. (Few of them had the necessary qualifications.)
answers: Few of the people who/that applied for the job had the necessary qualifications.

items.prompt: Amy showed me a picture of her son. (Her son is a police officer.)
answers: Amy showed me a picture of her son, who is a police officer.

exercises.instruction: Are the sentences OK? Correct them (and put in commas) where necessary. If the sentence is correct, write ‘OK’.

items.prompt: Anna told me about her new job that she’s enjoying very much.
answers: Anna told me about her new job, which she’s enjoying very much.

items.prompt: My office that is on the second floor is very small.
answers: My office, which is on the second floor, is very small.

items.prompt: The office that I’m using at the moment is very small.
answers: OK

items.prompt: Sarah’s father that used to be in the army now works for a TV company.
answers: Sarah’s father, who used to be in the army, now works for a TV company.

items.prompt: The doctor that examined me couldn’t find anything wrong.
answers: OK

items.prompt: The sun that is one of millions of stars in the universe provides us with heat and light.
answers: The sun, which is one of millions of stars in the universe, provides us with heat and light.
